input: Ask my doctor about iron deficiency test results

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which specific markers or results (e.g. ferritin, hemoglobin, serum iron) to ask about determines how focused and prepared the conversation needs to be.
Whether the appointment is already scheduled, upcoming, or still needs to be booked completely changes what the immediate next step is.
Whether this is an in-person visit, a phone call, or a patient portal message affects how the user should prepare and communicate.
Knowing whether this is the user's primary care doctor, a specialist (e.g. hematologist), or another provider affects the level of detail and type of questions to prepare.
If the user has a hard deadline (e.g. symptoms worsening, a follow-up window closing), that urgency shapes how quickly this needs to happen.
Some people want a full list of questions prepared in advance; others just need a single reminder note — knowing their preferred preparation style shapes the plan.
The user's end goal — whether it's understanding the results, getting a diagnosis, starting treatment, or getting a referral — defines what a successful conversation looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Ask doctor about iron deficiency test results
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to follow up with their doctor regarding iron deficiency test results, but key details about timing, format, and what specifically to ask are unclear.

questions.title: Which specific test results do you want to discuss?
questions.description: Identify the exact markers or panels the user wants to ask about, such as ferritin levels, hemoglobin, serum iron, or the full iron panel.

questions.title: Do you already have an appointment booked?
questions.description: Determine whether the user needs to schedule an appointment first or is preparing for an existing one.

questions.title: Will this be in-person, by phone, or via a patient portal?
questions.description: Clarify the communication channel so the preparation format (written questions vs. verbal notes) can be matched accordingly.

questions.title: Is this your GP or a specialist you are seeing?
questions.description: Knowing the type of doctor helps tailor the depth and technical level of the questions the user should prepare.

questions.title: Is there a deadline or urgency driving this follow-up?
questions.description: Understand whether symptoms, a treatment window, or a required callback date makes timing critical.

questions.title: Do you want a structured list of questions to bring?
questions.description: Find out whether the user wants a written question list prepared in advance or just a simple reminder to follow up.

questions.title: What outcome do you need from this conversation?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is to understand the results, confirm a diagnosis, begin treatment, or get referred to a specialist.
